newsitem.title: HONG KONG: U.S. dollar firm, local money quiet in Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: U.S. dollar firm, local money quiet in Hong Kong.

text.p: The U.S. dollar firmed in Hong Kong against both the yen and the mark on Wednesday, with dealers predicting further strength in the afternoon.
"Dollar-yen and dollar-mark are both having a good session," said one dealer.
The U.S. dollar was trading at 122.67 yen and 1.71 German marks, and there reports a major U.S. house was buying dollars aggressively against the mark.
The Hong Kong dollar was flat at HK$7.7430 while overnight money was at 4.38 percent.
Currency forwards were at 20 basis points in the three-month and 47 points in the six-month.
The three-month Hong Kong dollar deposit was at 5.60 percent against the U.S. three-month at 5.18 percent for a spread of 42 basis points.
The two-year Hong Kong Exchange Fund Note (EFN) yield was 5.96 percent against the U.S. two-year at 6.11 percent for a spread of 15 basis points.
The 10-year EFN yield was 7.18 percent against the U.S. 10-year at 6.58 percent for a spread of 60 basis points.
Among other yields, the three-year was at 6.28 percent, the five-year was at 6.73 percent, the seven-year was at 6.99 percent at the one-week was at 4.74 percent.
